harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, created the datauser account and a dedicated 512MB loopback-mounted XFS filesystem at /srv/data (backed by /var/lib/srv-data.img, persisted in /etc/fstab with loop,uquota options). Set an XFS user quota of 100MB (soft=hard=100m) for datauser via xfs_quota, so the limit is enforced natively by the filesystem's kernel-level quota subsystem rather than any application logic. Verified enforcement both before and after a full node reboot (writes past 100MB fail with "Disk quota exceeded"; writes under the limit succeed). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and quota/data state, issued systemctl reboot, polled until node1 reconnected, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed /srv/data auto-remounted with quota intact and data preserved.
actions_performed: Confirmed root fs is XFS with 'noquota' — chose a dedicated loopback XFS filesystem for /srv/data instead of altering root mount options
Installed the quota userspace tools (quota package) on node1
Created datauser account (useradd -m datauser)
Created 512MB image /var/lib/srv-data.img, formatted as XFS
Added persistent fstab entry: /var/lib/srv-data.img /srv/data xfs loop,uquota 0 0 (backed up original fstab to /etc/fstab.bak)
Mounted /srv/data with usrquota active, chowned to datauser
Set XFS user quota: bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota
Verified enforcement: write of 150MB truncated at exactly 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded'; write of 10MB succeeded
Captured baseline boot_id, mount state, data, and quota report before restart
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec became available again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart
Re-verified /srv/data mount, quota config, and data survived reboot
Re-verified quota enforcement still blocks over-limit writes after reboot, then cleaned up test file

evidence.summary: useradd -m datauser succeeded; id datauser shows uid=1000(datauser)

evidence.requirement: /srv/data quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (not app-level)
evidence.summary: Built dedicated XFS loopback filesystem, persisted in fstab with uquota option, mounted, and set XFS user quota bsoft=bhard=100M for datauser via xfs_quota
150MB write as datauser truncated at exactly 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded'; separate 10MB write under the limit succeeded and quota report reflected usage
Captured boot_id 34027437-307c-4f58-bdb2-1fe626bb2d66, confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota, data present, and quota report showing 10M/100M
systemctl reboot dispatched in background; command returned pid before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot (connection timeouts), then reconnected with new boot_id 8e10fe6f-7eb2-4f9d-a94d-4f9a64233ef5, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of quota-enforced filesystem and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab with usrquota, prior file (small.bin) intact, quota report unchanged, and over-limit write again failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' confirming enforcement survived the restart
